messages:
Maria: quick AM async — what I did / blockers / today:
- Did: landed the alert-reroute PR and adjusted debounce on 504 alerts
- Blocker: canary still flapping with intermittent 504s from backend node-7, can't repro locally
- Today: need traces + decision on canary ramping; will watch next rollout

Ashwin: grabbing traces now. noticed a burst of requests hitting the batcher queue ~02:15 UTC, looks correlated with higher seq lengths. pasted the grep snippet I ran:
```
grep -E 'node-7.*504|batcher.*latency' /var/logs/proxy.log | tail -n 40
```
will attach full trace shortly

sre-bot: Incident watch: new ticket created INC-1234 for repeated 504s (owner: Ashwin). Link: https://tickets.internal/INC-1234 :rotating_light:

Olivia: I merged a small noise-tuning change to the alert rules (threshold +1%) — should cut the chatter. Also updated the runbook note about retry/backoff for rpc timeouts.

Dave: FYI I'm planning a low-risk rollout for the KV-evict tweak at 23:00 UTC tonight (canary -> 2% -> 5% -> 50%). If node-7 keeps misbehaving, hold the rollout. I'll put a calendar block.

Maria: thanks. suspicious part: logs show repeated `rpc timeout` when talking to model-host-prod in us-west-2 from node-7. could be egress rule or intermittent throttling upstream.

Ashwin: confirmed — node-7 had ~20x retries in a 10m window. I spun up a pcap on the node and will check network metrics. Opening the ticket with the initial hypothesis.

Olivia: quick ask for oncall: @oncall can you ack the ticket and be available during the 23:00 canary window? if we need to roll back quickly we'd want someone to own the rollback. :eyes:

Dave: I'll be the active oncall for that window and can cut the canary if we get >5% error delta. Also added a fallback routing rule to re-route traffic to the secondary model shard if latency spikes.

Maria: question — do we want to ramp to 5% immediately to get more signal or stick with the planned 2% then ramp? pros: faster signal; cons: could amplify the fault. thoughts?

Ashwin: prefer ramp plan: start 2%, wait 10m, then 5% if no errors. also add a tiny pause between steps so autoscaler doesn't react to short bursts.

Olivia: agree with Ashwin. I also committed a quick synthetic test to the repo: `./scripts/synthetic_load.sh --seq 512 --concurrency 20` — run that pre-canary to catch obvious failures.

sre-bot: Reminder — maintenance window/announced deploy 22:45-23:30 UTC in the infra calendar.

Maria: perfect. I'll monitor logs and post another update at 23:10 after the first canary step. ping me if anyone sees fresh 504s before then. :thumbsup:
